# Oncology

We understand that a cancer diagnosis in your pet can be emotional and overwhelming. Fortunately, the field of veterinary oncology has progressed tremendously over the past several years. AESC’s medical oncology service provides advanced diagnostics and treatments for pets with various tumor types. We work together with your family, your primary care veterinarian, and even other board-certified specialists in our hospital to provide your pet with the most compassionate, comprehensive care possible.

### Potential signs of cancer in pets

  * Masses, especially those that grow rapidly, feel firm, or change in appearance (e.g. bruising or bleeding)

  * Dramatic weight loss

  * Swelling of the abdomen, particularly in conjunction with pale gums, decreased energy, and/or collapse

  * Sudden pain, limping, or swelling of a limb

  * Blood and/or foul odor coming from the nose or mouth

  * Major change in appetite

  * Persistent vomiting

  * Diarrhea

### Commonly treated cancers in pets

  * Lymphoma

  * Osteosarcoma

  * Mast cell tumors

  * Anal sac adenocarcinoma

  * Hemangiosarcoma

  * Soft tissue sarcoma

  * Transitional cell carcinoma (bladder tumor)

  * Melanoma

  * Mammary carcinoma

### Diagnostics

  * Complete blood count (CBC), blood chemistry, and urinalysis

Advanced diagnostic imaging

  * Digital radiography

  * Ultrasound

  * Computed tomography (CT)

  * MRI

>   * Cytology

  * Tumor marker testing

  * Soft tissue and bone biopsies

### Treatments

Chemotherapy

  * Chemotherapy may be used to treat cancer that cannot be removed with surgery, or it may be used to enhance the effectiveness of surgery. Fortunately, pets tolerate chemotherapy quite well. In veterinary medicine, chemotherapy is dosed to limit side effects as much as possible so that your pet maintains an excellent quality of life. Our oncologist can also adjust protocols and dosages to reduce unwanted side effects. If after treatment, vomiting, diarrhea, or decreased appetite occurs, these symptoms can be managed with take-home medications. Should side effects need any additional treatment after hours, our emergency service is available 24/7/365.

  * Surgical removal of tumors

>   * Chemotherapy is not the only option for cancer treatment. Our oncologist works closely alongside our board-certified surgeons and board-certified radiologists to determine if tumors can safely and effectively be surgically removed. For some cancers, follow-up chemotherapy is still recommended after surgery, but for many other cancers, surgical removal provides a cure.

Image: Headshot of Janet Lori

# Janet Lori

### DVM, MS, DACVIM (Oncology)

A native of Dallas, Texas, Dr. Lori earned her undergraduate degree in veterinary science at Texas A&M University. She then graduated from A&M’s College of Veterinary Medicine in 2005. She moved from Texas to Colorado State University, where she completed a one-year small animal medicine and surgery rotating internship, as well as a residency program in small animal oncology. Dr. Lori became board-certified in internal medicine (Oncology) through the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine in 2010, and also completed her Masters of Clinical Science.

Dr. Lori joined the crew at AESC as our staff oncologist in August, 2011. Dr. Lori enjoys all things oncology, with a particular interest in the new and exciting options available for the treatment of mast cell tumors.

# About Us

Image: Colorado Veterinary Medical Association (CVMA) Proud Member

## What is a Veterinary Specialist?

A board-certified veterinary specialist is a veterinarian who focuses on one area of medicine by completing at least four years of additional training in a specific discipline. Then, after conducting original research and passing a rigorous certifying examination, he or she becomes recognized by a specialty organization sanctioned by the American Veterinary Medical Association.

Recent medical developments and available treatments have grown at a tremendous rate, making it virtually impossible for a veterinarian to maintain expertise in all disciplines of medicine. The increasing complexity of veterinary medical care has led to the development of specialized training programs. With their advanced training and knowledge, veterinary specialists can provide truly exceptional care for their patients.

Animal Emergency & Specialty Center (AESC) is a specialty and 24/7/365 emergency veterinary hospital. Our team of highly skilled and specialized veterinarians, certified technicians , and support staff provide advanced medical care for your pet's emergencies and complex health needs.

AESC is comprised of board-certified specialists across various medical disciplines. When your pet experiences a health issue that requires a high level of specialization, your family veterinarian will refer you to a specialty hospital like AESC for further care. At AESC, your pet will have access to multiple specialists who are experts in their respective fields. Working closely with you and your family veterinarian, we form the third essential component of your pet's healthcare team by providing advanced diagnostic and treatment options beyond the scope of routine general care.

## Our History

> ### AESC Founded (2001)

AESC was founded in 2001 by veterinarians who recognized a need for after-hours veterinary care in the Parker/Franktown/Elizabeth areas. The original location was less than 1,000 square feet and located on Parker Road at Plaza Drive. Within a year, the demand for care grew and AESC expanded its service to include Surgery in addition to 24/7/365 Emergency Care.

### Opening (2004)

By 2004, AESC had outgrown the original facility and opened the doors to the current location. At the new location, we treated 200-400 emergency patients per month and expanded into specialty services like Critical Care and Diagnostic Imaging. Over the years, we added Internal Medicine with non-invasive endoscopic procedures, Oncology with a wide range of chemotherapy options, Rehabilitation with an underwater treadmill, and Neurology with an MRI scanner.

### Renovations (2020-2021)

In 2020-2021, AESC underwent a major renovation to grow the facility to 20,000 square feet. This expansion included a new 16-slice GE Brightspeed CT scanner, mobile fluoroscopy unit, four additional surgery suites, and a more capable 23X MRI scanner. In addition, we added a 1000 square foot workspace for our rehabilitation team including two underwater treadmills and a brand-new oncology ward.

### Today

Today we continue to grow and strive to offer a comprehensive array of services and the best patient care available in the area. Our most recent service additions include a board-certified anesthesiologist and two additional board-certified radiologists.
